title: Polygon Vocabulary Practice
description: Practice defining polygon vocabulary and identifying examples, non-examples, sides, vertices, diagonals, regular polygons, and irregular polygons.

questions.question: Which description best defines a polygon?
options: A closed plane figure made only of straight line segments
Any figure with at least one angle
An open figure made of straight and curved parts
questions.explanation: A polygon must be closed and made only of straight line segments.

questions.question: What is a vertex of a polygon?
options: A straight line segment on the boundary
A corner where two sides meet
questions.explanation: A vertex is a corner formed where two sides of a polygon meet.

questions.question: A circle is a polygon because it is closed.
questions.explanation: A circle is closed, but it has a curved boundary. Polygons must have only straight sides.

questions.question: In pentagon ABCDE, which segment is a diagonal?
questions.explanation: A and C are non-adjacent vertices in pentagon ABCDE, so AC is a diagonal. AB, BC, and CD are sides.

questions.question: A polygon with all sides equal and all angles equal is called a ____ polygon.
questions.explanation: A regular polygon has both equal side lengths and equal angle measures.

questions.question: Which figure is a non-example of a polygon?
options: A shape with one curved side
questions.explanation: A figure with a curved side is not a polygon because polygon sides must be straight line segments.

questions.question: An irregular polygon can still be a polygon.
questions.explanation: Irregular means the polygon does not have all sides and all angles equal. It can still be closed and made of straight sides.

questions.question: Explain why a square is a regular polygon.
questions.correctAnswer: A square is a regular polygon because it is closed, has straight sides, all four sides are equal, and all four angles are equal.
questions.explanation: A complete explanation should mention that a square is a polygon and that both its sides and angles are equal.
